### Observed differences

- In the later window, A21 and A22 occur later in traces (mean position A21 from about 0.51 to 0.62; A22 from about 0.36 to 0.48), while A30, A31, A36 and A37 occur earlier (means from about 0.58 to about 0.41). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- For every pair of A21 or A22 with A30, A31, A36 or A37, the order reversed: before, A21/A22 preceded the other activity in about 100% of cases; after, the other activity precedes A21/A22 in about 98% of cases. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008]
- A21's outgoing transitions changed from a split among A30, A31, A36 and A37 to almost always A25 (about 98%). [DIR002]
- A20's outgoing transitions changed from almost always A22 to a split among A30, A31, A36 and A37, with A22 nearly disappearing as a successor. [DIR001]
- A30, A31, A36 and A37 now sometimes go to A22 (about 19–30% of transitions) and almost never to A25 (down from about 22–32% to about 1%). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- The distance between A20 and A22 changed from adjacent (lag 1 in 100%) to far apart (lag 5 in 98%); the distance between A21 and A25 changed from far apart (lag 5 in 100%) to adjacent (lag 1 in 98%). [LAG001, LAG002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a reordering in which A21 and A22 moved from before the group A30/A31/A36/A37 to after it, and A25 moved from after that group to immediately after A21. The direct relational reversal for all eight pairs, the positional shifts, and the successor changes are consistent with this single structural reordering. [REL001-REL008, POS001-POS006, DIR001-DIR006, LAG001-LAG002]

A competing explanation based only on sampling differences in variant frequencies is unlikely to account for the consistency of the order reversal across independent indicators, although some lag items have only four supporting traces in the later window and are therefore weak on their own. [LAG003-LAG008]
